text:
mira: Heads-up — saw a perf regression in the RAG canary after yesterday's kernel swap. P95 for /generate-chat jumped from 220ms -> 390ms on small-ctx (1k tokens) workloads. :thinking_face:
ashwin: ugh. reproable on canary only or in prod too?
mira: only canary so far. perf-bot posted metrics: 
perf-bot: canary: /generate-chat p50 85ms p95 390ms p99 820ms, cache hit-rate 0.34 (was 0.61 before swap).
jen: throwing in profiler dump from a few requests (RAG prompt, structured JSON output) — looks like KV cache misses spiked during prefix lookup. pasted snippet: ```
prefix_key_lookup: 0.002s (misses 66%)
kv_fetch_shard: 0.018s (alloc spikes)
kernel_dispatch_wait: 0.09s
```
mira: interesting that structured outputs (we return JSON blobs) have worse hit-rate than plain text prompts. could be keying mismatch.
ashwin: did we change normalization for structured templates? We recently added metadata headers to the convo prefix on canary. If those are in the cache key, cardinality explodes.
jen: I ran an offline key-collation on a sample of 10k traces:
- chat (plain): unique prefix keys per 1k requests = 87
- chat (structured JSON templates): unique prefix keys per 1k requests = 642
- completion short: unique keys per 1k = 230
- RAG long: unique keys per 1k = 980
hit-rate estimates map to those numbers roughly.
mira: ah ok. so adding metadata in-line is killing cacheing. we need deterministic key normalization before we change kernel stacks.
nashwin: propose patch: strip per-request headers + canonicalize whitespace + sort unordered metadata keys before hashing. quick diff: ```diff
- key = hash(prefix_bytes + meta_bytes)
+ meta_norm = sort_keys(strip_timestamps(meta))
+ key = hash(prefix_bytes + meta_norm)
```
samops: note — storage TTL and eviction policy also matter. canary has LRU window set to 30m; production is 6h. if key cardinality jumps, smaller window = immediate miss storms.
jen: good catch. I measured memory churn — when misses spike we see kernel_dispatch_wait up because we rebuild KV on the fly and re-quantize kv blocks. trace: ```
[trace] kv_rebuild: 0.12s -> causes extra 4MB GPU allocs repeatedly
```
mira: two short-term mitigations: 1) revert metadata in prefix 2) bump canary LRU to 2h + enable soft-prefetch for first token on RAG routes.
nashwin: about soft-prefetch — proposing batching tweak too: when request arrives and cache miss predicted (low past hit-rate), coalesce nearby requests in 50ms micro-batch and precompute KV for the merged prefix vector. config snippet: ```yaml
batching:
  microbatch_ms: 50
  prefer_prefetch_on_miss: true
```
jen: did a microbench: coalescing + soft-prefetch reduced p95 back to ~240ms in simulated canary traces (still slightly higher than baseline but acceptable).
mira: longer-term: we should separate cache keys for 'structural' template parts vs ephemeral per-request data. store a two-level key: template_id -> ephemeral suffix. that keeps template-level hits high.
samops: agree. also watch kernel selection interplay: some kernels re-order kv layout (for quantized shards) and that can change rebuild cost. want to add kernel dispatch tags to tracing so we can correlate per-kernel rebuild time. small trace example: ```
kernel=v2.quant_block reorder=true kv_rebuild=0.13s
kernel=v1.base reorder=false kv_rebuild=0.04s
```
nashwin: okay will instrument that. plan: 1) rollback prefix metadata change on canary (now) 2) enable LRU=2h on canary (in 10m) 3) deploy key-normalization patch to staging 4) run 24h warmup job with synthetic RAG templates + measure hit-rate and p95.
jen: I'll own the synthetic workload; will create structured JSON templates that vary only in ephemeral fields so we can verify two-level keying helps.
mira: assign playbook tasks in the canary thread and tag perf-alert if p95 > 350ms after changes.
nashwin: one more note — completions-only routes show different behavior: their prefix keys are shorter and reuse prefix cache well, but batching heuristics sometimes delay small completion requests (tiny prompts) because coalescing threshold was tuned for chat. we'll tweak thresholds per-route.
junior-dev: quick question — is there a simple test I can run locally to see key normalization effects?
jen: run: ```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python tools/key_collate.py --sample traces/last_1k.json --normalize --report
```
will spit out collision rates and suggested normalization operations.
mira: thanks everyone. I'll roll the rollback and LRU bump now, ping when observability shows hit-rate recovering. :thumbsup:
